issues.issue: What is the legislative purpose of s. 117 of the IRPA (people smuggling offence)?
issues.applicant_position: Purpose is narrow: it targets organized smuggling, not humanitarian, mutual or family assistance.
issues.respondent_position: Purpose is to catch all acts that in any way assist entry of undocumented migrants.
issues.result_quote: the purpose of s. 117 is to criminalize the smuggling of people into Canada in the context of organized crime

issues.issue: Does s. 117 violate s. 7 of the Charter because it is overbroad?
issues.applicant_position: Section 117 reaches humanitarian, mutual and family aid outside its purpose, so it is overbroad under s. 7.
issues.respondent_position: Attorney General consent under s. 117(4) screens out improper prosecutions, so no overbreadth.
issues.result_quote: I conclude that s. 117 of the IRPA is overbroad.

issues.issue: Does s. 117 violate s. 7 through gross disproportionality, vagueness or inequality?
issues.applicant_position: Section 117 is grossly disproportionate, vague and unequal, contrary to the principles of fundamental justice.
issues.result_quote: In view of my conclusion that s. 117 is overbroad, I find it unnecessary to consider these arguments.

issues.issue: Is the s. 7 infringement justified under s. 1 of the Charter?
issues.applicant_position: The overbreadth is not a reasonable limit; the Crown has not shown a demonstrable justification.
issues.respondent_position: Objective is pressing; law is minimally impairing because no better alternative existed.
issues.result_quote: The Crown has not satisfied its burden under s. 1 .

issues.issue: What is the appropriate remedy for the unconstitutional s. 117: strike down or read down?
issues.applicant_position: Strike down s. 117 in its entirety as unconstitutional.
issues.result_quote: I conclude that the preferable remedy is to read down s. 117 as not applicable to persons who give humanitarian, mutual or family assistance.
